newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch -April 11.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch -April 11.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading.
* The Philippine stock market is likely to extend its technical rebound on Friday, although brokers said the recovery will be short-lived due to absence of buying incentives.
* Asian Capital Equities analyst Leila Calderon said the technical rally may be sustained as investors have started picking up oversold issues, especially on the banking and property counters.
But investors were still waiting for the release of first quarter results before taking a firmer stand on the market, Calderon said.
* Abacus Securities research head Erwin Tan said he saw the index meeting its resistance at 3,100 over the next few days.
He said the recent drop in banking and property issues should provide buying opportunities as their valuations had gone down considerably.
* Sun Hung Kai Securities remained wary of the break in the seven-session decline.
"A reversal from the bearish mode can be confirmed if the 2,880 support is maintained and foreign hands re-enter the market," an outlook by Sun Hung Kai Securities Inc said.
* Philippine Asia Equity Securities Inc trader Mike Julian said he encouraged investors to accumulate select index heavyweights and secondliners.
"Most of these issues are fundamentally sound and are bound to recover. Buying of bargain-priced index stocks PLDT, Filinvest Land Inc, and Philippine National Bank is recommended," Julian said.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index closed on Thursday at 2,949.02 points, up 39.72 or 1.37 percent, on a technical rebound. PLDT's ADR's rose 50 cents to close at $58.25.
* The Dow Jones dropped 23.79 points to 6,540.05 points on Thursday.
* Outgoing Bankers Association of the Philippines president Rafael Buenaventura says fears over rising default in real estate and consumer loans are unfounded.
* La Tondena Distillers Inc has set an expansion programme of 2.5 to 2.7 billion pesos this year, vice president Joseph John Ong says.
* Globe Telecom GMCR said the rate rebalancing plan of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co will hurt new local exchange carriers.
